fullPassage: A professor had students craft poetry-generating programs. The children would feed the program verbs, adjectives, and nouns, and the computer would combine them into lines of poetry: "MAD WOLF HATES BECAUSE INSANE WOLF SKIPS" or "UGLY MAN LOVES BECAUSE UGLY DOG HATES." The process of trying to get the program to work lent students startling insights into language. Jenny, a thirteen-year-old girl who had previously earned only mediocre grades, came in one day and announced, "Now I know why we have nouns and verbs." She'd been taught grammar and the parts of speech for years without understanding them. But as Jenny struggled to get the program to work, she realized she had to classify words into categories—all the verbs in one bucket, all the nouns in another—or else the sentences the computer spat out wouldn't make sense. Grammar suddenly became deeply meaningful. This produced another effect: Jenny began getting A's in her language classes.

The children would feed the program verbs, adjectives, and nouns, and the computer would combine them into lines of poetry: "MAD WOLF HATES BECAUSE INSANE WOLF SKIPS" or "UGLY MAN LOVES BECAUSE UGLY DOG HATES." The process of trying to get the program to work lent students <u>startling</u> insights into language. Jenny, a thirteen-year-old girl who had previously earned only mediocre grades, came in one day and announced, "Now I know why we have nouns and verbs." She'd been taught grammar and the parts of speech for years without understanding them. But as Jenny struggled to get the program to work, she realized she had to classify words into categories—all the verbs in one bucket, all the nouns in another—or else the sentences the computer spat out wouldn't make sense. Grammar suddenly became deeply meaningful. This produced another effect: Jenny began getting A's in her language classes.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 startling의 의미와 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: 학생들에게 놀라운(startling) 언어 통찰을 주었다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① surprising(놀라운): 동의어
❌ ② amazing(놀라운): 동의어
❌ ③ exciting(흥미진진한): 긍정 계열 동의어
✅ ④ predictable(예측 가능한): startling의 반의어. 놀람 없는 뻔한 상태
det.tip: startling ↔ predictable — 놀라운 vs 뻔한.

questions.passage:
(A) She filled the <u>bucket</u> with water from the well and carried it to the garden to water the flowers.

(B) Jenny realized she had to classify words into categories — all the verbs in one <u>bucket</u>, all the nouns in another — or the sentences wouldn't make sense.
questions.stem: (A)와 (B)의 밑줄 친 bucket의 문맥적 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) filled with water — 실제 물을 담는 양동이. (B) classify words into categories — 분류 개념상의 '범주/분류함'.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 둘 다 양동이는 (B)의 'classify into categories' 맥락과 불일치
✅ ② (A) 양동이 — (B) 범주/분류함: (A)는 실제 용기, (B)는 추상적 분류 단위를 비유적 bucket로 표현
❌ ③ 정반대 해석
❌ ④ (A)의 fill with water와 범주 해석은 모순
det.tip: bucket의 비유적 용법 — 범주/분류함(category)을 일상 용어로 표현.

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "extremely surprising or unexpected"

det.korean: 매우 놀랍거나 예상치 못한 상태.
det.analysis:
✅ ① startling(놀라운): '매우 놀랍거나 예상치 못한'의 직접 대응어
❌ ② mediocre(평범한)은 평균/보통의 속성
❌ ③ meaningful(의미 있는)은 의미의 속성이지 놀람 아님
❌ ④ deeply(깊이): 부사로 정도를 표현
det.tip: startling은 surprising보다 더 '깜짝 놀랄 정도의' 강도를 가진 형용사.

questions.passage: She __________ (have) been taught grammar and the parts of speech for years without understanding them.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로, 1단어)

det.korean: 그녀는 수년간 문법과 품사를 배워왔지만 이해하지는 못했다.
det.analysis: 현재완료 수동태 'had been taught' 구조가 필요. have의 과거형 had + been + p.p. 구조. 문맥 과거 서사 시제 일치.
det.tip: had been + p.p. = 과거완료 수동. have → had (과거형), 뒤의 been taught와 결합해 '~해져 왔었다'.

questions.passage: This produced another effect: Jenny began __________ (get) A's in her language classes.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로, 1단어)

det.korean: 이것은 또 다른 효과를 낳았다: Jenny는 언어 수업에서 A를 받기 시작했다.
det.analysis: begin + V-ing(동명사) 패턴. get의 -ing 형태는 getting(자음 중복). '시작하다 + 행위'는 동명사 또는 to부정사 모두 가능하나 원문은 동명사 형태.
det.tip: begin + 동명사/to부정사 모두 가능. get → getting (자음 2개 중첩).

det.korean: Jenny가 어느 날 와서 선언한 말: '____'. 그녀는 수년간 문법을 배워도 이해 못 했었다.
